headline: Highest risk is low: both docs-only prompt repositories have no runnable surfaces, so interaction pathways are largely absent.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Both profiles are non-runnable content-writing repositories with empty io_surfaces and no documented ingestion path between them. Without a shared channel, there is no plausible default prompt-injection bridge. The pairwise pathway is therefore blocked by the profiles as given.
conditions: IF either profile is later connected through copy-paste, shared files, or an MCP bridge, reassess injection risk.
mitigations: Keep the repositories isolated from any shared clipboard or workspace.
Do not wire either repo into an agent that auto-parses repository content as instructions.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging if a shared channel is introduced.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Neither profile touches data classes, and both are docs-only repositories with no io_surfaces. Agent B explicitly has network_egress:none, so there is no documented exfiltration path. Agent A has no documented data flow at all, so leakage between the pair is not plausible from the profiles.
conditions: IF either agent is later given access to sensitive files or a shared workspace, re-evaluate leakage.
mitigations: Avoid placing sensitive files in any directory both agents can read.
Keep Agent B's network egress disabled.
requires-engineering: add workspace isolation if shared storage is introduced.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: No overlapping write-capable surfaces are documented. Agent A has empty capabilities and io_surfaces, while Agent B only documents network_egress:none and likewise no write surfaces. With no shared mutable resource, capability conflict is provably absent in the current profiles.
conditions: IF either agent gains filesystem, git, database, or OAuth write scopes, reassess for conflicts.
mitigations: Do not grant shared write access to the same directory.
Keep both agents read-only in any future integration.
requires-engineering: introduce locking if mutable shared resources are added.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Neither profile is runnable, and neither exposes action-taking authority or output channels that another agent could treat as authoritative. Agent A and Agent B are both content-writing repositories, but the profiles do not document any downstream automation. The cascade pathway is therefore not established.
conditions: IF one agent's output is later consumed as authoritative input by an action-taking system, reassess cascading error.
mitigations: Require human review before any downstream action uses generated content.
Do not auto-execute commands from repository text.
requires-engineering: add verification gates before any future automation.

E_compliance.rationale: The profiles show no data classes touched, no residency metadata, and no compliance-sensitive processing. Agent A and Agent B are both docs-only open-source repositories, so there is no documented compliance mismatch to assess. The other agent is not separately cited because no regulated data flow exists.
conditions: IF regulated data is introduced into either repository workflow, reassess residency and retention obligations.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of both workflows.
Document any future retention or residency requirements before integration.
requires-engineering: add compliance controls if the pair is repurposed for regulated data.
